title: 12 Thames Road London Borough Of Barking & Dagenham: Geoarchaeological & Palaeoenvironmental Assessment Report
description: Geoarchaeological Fieldwork and deposit model Borehole survey and updated geoarchaeological deposit model Palaeoenvironmental assessment (sediment characterisation, radiocarbon dating, OSL dating, pollen, diatom, macrofossils) Palaeoenvironmental analysis (further OSL dating, diatom and microfaunal investigation) On the western side of the site, the gravel surface is overlain by a sequence of alluvial and peat deposits capped by Made Ground. Peat formation was recorded as taking place from the early Neolithic to late Bronze Age. Both the timing of peat formation and vegetation communities indicated by an assessment of the pollen are broadly consistent with previous palaeoenvironmental reconstructions undertaken in the local vicinity at Barking Riverside. The evolution of the landscape on the eastern part of the site was different. The gravel is recorded at a lower elevation and the alluvial and peat deposits are seemingly absent. Instead, thick deposits of silts and sands are recorded, which are often soft, mottled in colour and sometimes laminated. These deposits are interpreted as the infill of a sizable north-south aligned palaeochannel traversing the eastern side of the site and possibly turning to the west towards the southern end of the site. OSL dating has shown that the entire sequence is of early medieval date. Diatom, foraminifera and ostracoda investigations indicate the channel would appear to have infilled under predominantly estuarine conditions. There is no doubt that the channel infilled after accumulation of the peat (and in all likelihood, after much if not all of the overlying alluvial deposits).
creator: Christopher Green
E Andrieux
J Athersuch
Rob Batchelor
Tom Hill
